body.statement:
For every admissible pair with \(2\leq n\leq5\), the exact sharp coordinate-degree frontier is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 n & D_k(n)\\ \hline
 2 & D_0(2)=1,\\
 3 & D_k(3)=1\quad(0\leq k\leq1),\\
 4 & D_k(4)=2\quad(0\leq k\leq3),\\
 5 & D_0(5)=2,\quad D_1(5)=3,\quad D_k(5)=4\quad(2\leq k\leq6).
\end{array}
\]
In each nontrivial lower-bound construction an original directed coefficient separates all generic conjugate branches.
body.proof_tex:
The admissible range is \(0\le k\le(n-1)(n-2)/2\).  For \(n=2\), it contains only \(k=0\), and \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) gives
\[
 D_0(2)=1.
\]

For \(n=3\), one has \(k\in\{0,1\}\).  The two-block conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:small\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maxima}\) gives \(d_e(G)\le1\) for every finite query.  Budget monotonicity follows directly from \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\): if \(j\le k\), then \(\mathcal G_{n,j}\subseteq\mathcal G_{n,k}\).  The tree witness \(D_0(3)=1\) therefore supplies the reverse inequality for both budgets, and
\[
 D_k(3)=1\qquad(0\le k\le1).
\tag{87}
\]

For \(n=4\), the three-block bound gives \(D_k(4)\le2\) for every admissible \(0\le k\le3\).  The separating degree-two tree witness in \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\), together with \(\mathcal G_{4,0}\subseteq\mathcal G_{4,k}\), gives the reverse inequality.  Hence
\[
 D_k(4)=2\qquad(0\le k\le3).
\tag{88}
\]

For \(n=5,k=0\), the tree lemma gives \(D_0(5)=2\).  When \(k=1\), the refined five-block calculation gives \(D_1(5)\le3\), while \(\mathrm{lem:five\mbox{-}node\mbox{-}cubic\mbox{-}coordinate\mbox{-}transfer}\) supplies a member of \(\mathcal G_{5,1}\) with an original edge of degree three.  Thus
\[
 D_1(5)=3.
\tag{89}
\]
For admissible \(k\ge2\), the four-block bound gives \(D_k(5)\le4\).  The proved quartic witness belongs to \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\), and budget monotonicity gives \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\subseteq\mathcal G_{5,k}\).  Therefore
\[
 D_k(5)=4\qquad(2\le k\le6).
\tag{90}
\]
Equations (87)--(90), together with the two-vertex case, give the displayed table.  The tree, cubic, and quartic lower-bound witnesses all query an original directed coefficient.  Their finite minimal polynomials are separable in characteristic zero, so the stated degree equals the number of distinct generic conjugate coordinate values and those coefficients separate all branches.
body.justification: The exact table removes every vertex size through five from the unresolved frontier.
